types.name: Redstone.Group
types.docstring:
Group

An [assembly](@ref g-assembly) written as a value, the form an assembly takes
unless domain code needs its type.

A `Group` is an assembly that holds its children and its declarations as field
values. The elements of its `children` field, a `NamedTuple` of
[components](@ref g-component), are its children. Its [`local_wires`](@ref),
[`input_wires`](@ref), [`output_wires`](@ref) and [`sample_times`](@ref) are
ordinary functions of the instance, which read its fields. A wire field holds
the [entries](@ref g-entry) or a function that computes them, as the
constructor states.

The one declaration it adds is [`transparent_container`](@ref). `children` is
[name-transparent](@ref g-container-children), so its elements go by bare key
everywhere a child name appears. That is `"ctl/out" => "plant/u"` for a wire,
`(ctl = Relative(2),)` for a rate, `at("ctl", …)` for a
[condition](@ref g-condition) prefix and `"plant"` for a read path, as in
`port(sim, "plant", :y)`. A `Group`'s declarations are then textually identical
to a named assembly's. The rate declaration's field-name sugar, keying on the
field rather than on a path segment, keeps working as
`(children = Relative(2),)` for the uniform case.

types.name: Redstone.Library.Junction
types.docstring:
Junction{In, Out, N}(f) -> Junction{In, Out, N}

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes a fold of its `N`
inputs as its one output.

The inputs `in1` to `inN` are typed `In`. The one output, `y`, is typed `Out`,
and a wire names it as in `"sum/y"`. It publishes `y = f(in1, …, inN)`, the
fold applied in positional order.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) is stateless. A user writes a
custom fold, such as a weighted blend or a mass-properties composition, at the
site.

The fold holds no state and declares no [events](@ref g-state-event). A
discontinuity written into it therefore lands wherever it falls inside a step. A
clamp is fine, since its kink is second-order downstream. So is a branch on a
`Bool` that flips at a [boundary](@ref g-boundary), as a saturation code does. A
branch on a continuous quantity makes a mode silently. The components with
modes, such as [`Relay`](@ref), declare one.

See also [`SumJunction`](@ref), [`Or`](@ref), [`And`](@ref), [`Pack`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.Unpack
types.docstring:
Unpack{V, N}() -> Unpack{V, N}

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes the `N` elements of
its `SVector` input as `N` outputs.

The one input, `u`, is an `SVector{N, V}`, and the outputs `out1` to `outN`
are typed `V`, with `outi = u[i]`. A wire names the input as in
`"unpack/u"`. The [library component](@ref g-library-component) is stateless,
and the inverse of [`Pack`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.Switch
types.docstring:
Switch{V}() -> Switch{V}

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes one of its two inputs,
picked by a `Bool` input.

The inputs `in1` and `in2` are typed `V` and `select` is a `Bool`. The one
output, `y`, is typed `V`. It is `in1` while `select` holds and `in2` otherwise.
The [library component](@ref g-library-component) is stateless.

The output reads all three inputs. A `select` wired from a memoryless function
of the output therefore closes an [algebraic loop](@ref g-algebraic-loop), which
the build refuses as `AlgebraicCycle`.

The component declares no [event](@ref g-state-event), so the jump in the output
lands where `select` flips. A `select` published from a mode, or held between
[ticks](@ref g-tick), flips on a [boundary](@ref g-boundary) and the jump is
clean. One computed from a continuous quantity inside a
[stage body](@ref g-stage-function) flips inside a step and smears that step.
That is a mode made silently. A [`Comparator`](@ref) on the quantity is the
declared way to produce `select`. A [`Relay`](@ref) publishes a value rather
than a `Bool`, so it reaches `select` through a [`Junction`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.StopRequest
types.docstring:
StopRequest(; reason = "") -> StopRequest

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes a
[stop request](@ref g-stop-request) while its `Bool` input holds.

Its one output, `y`, is a [`StopFlag`](@ref). It publishes `STOP_REQUESTED`
while its one input, the `Bool` `u`, holds and `NO_STOP` otherwise. The
[library component](@ref g-library-component) is stateless, so it refreshes at
every [boundary](@ref g-boundary) and sits anywhere in the tree.

Any [component](@ref g-component) may publish a request, since the request is
the [port](@ref g-port)'s type.

# Keywords

- `reason`: the reason the component's requests report, read by
  [`stop_reason`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.Constant
types.docstring:
Constant(value) -> Constant

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes a fixed value, with no
inputs and no state.

Its one output, `y`, publishes `value` from [stage 1](@ref g-stage-function).
The [library component](@ref g-library-component) is stateless, so discrete
consumers read it as well.

The output is [pinned](@ref g-walked) at the parameter `V`, the type of `value`.
It carries zero partials under every `Dual` [activation](@ref g-activation). A
consumer input declared plain `Float64`, which admits a value with or without
partials, accepts it as a value that never carries partials.

The value is a field, not an overridable default. A source set from outside is a
[root input](@ref g-root-input).

See also [`Source`](@ref), [`Step`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.Step
types.docstring:
Step(; t_step, before = 0.0, after = 1.0, localized::Bool = true) -> Step

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes one value before a
given time and another from then on.

Its one output, `y`, publishes `before` until `t_step` and `after` from then on.
The [library component](@ref g-library-component) has no inputs and no
continuous state. Its one mode, the field `m`, picks the value. One
[state event](@ref g-state-event), `fire`, sets it once `t` reaches `t_step`.

`before` and `after` broadcast to one shape and type, the parameter `V`,
`Float64` or an `SArray` of `Float64`, so a scalar pairs with a vector and
integer values qualify. The output is [pinned](@ref g-walked) at `V`. It carries
zero partials under every [activation](@ref g-activation), as a
[`Constant`](@ref)'s does.

`localized` picks the detection policy.
[Localized](@ref g-localized), the step ends at the crossing and the jump lands
there. [Non-localized](@ref g-non-localized), the event fires at the end of the
step in which it was first observed. The jump then lands on the first
[boundary](@ref g-boundary) at or after `t_step`, never inside a step.

A `t_step` at or before `t₀` fires at [boundary zero](@ref g-boundary-zero), and
the output publishes `after` from the start.

# Keywords

- `t_step`: the time of the step, any time.
- `before`: the value before `t_step`.
- `after`: the value from `t_step` on.
- `localized`: `true` for a localized step, `false` for a non-localized one.

types.name: Redstone.Library.Source
types.docstring:
Source{V}(f) -> Source{V}
    Source(f) -> Source{Float64}

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes a function of time,
with no inputs and no state.

Its one output, `y`, publishes `f(t)` from [stage 1](@ref g-stage-function).
`Source(f)` is `Source{Float64}(f)`. `f` receives the plain `Float64` time under
`Float64` and a one-layer `Dual` [activation](@ref g-activation), so it need not
be generic there. It returns a `V`. Nothing converts, so a value of another type
is refused as `ConformanceFailure`, at build for the value the build reads and
as a `StepError` carrying it on a later [frame](@ref g-frame).

The output is [pinned](@ref g-walked) at `V` and carries zero partials under
every activation. The time loses one `Dual` layer before `f` sees it. At a
nested `Dual`, an `f` that returns the inner `Dual` is refused at build as
`ConformanceFailure`.

A source set from outside is a [root input](@ref g-root-input).

See also [`Constant`](@ref), [`Step`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.GaussianWhiteNoise
types.docstring:
GaussianWhiteNoise(; seed, μ = nothing, σ = nothing, psd = nothing) -> GaussianWhiteNoise

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes a seeded Gaussian white
noise sample at each [tick](@ref g-tick).

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) is a discrete Gaussian white
noise process. At each tick, its one output, `y`, publishes an independent
sample of mean `μ` and standard deviation `σ`. It publishes from
[stage 1](@ref g-stage-function).

The sample is a pure function of `seed` and the tick count. The tick count is
the one [store](@ref g-store) value, the field `s`, written `k` below.
[Replay](@ref g-replay) therefore reproduces the stream. After a tick the store
holds the next sample's index, so `k` reads `N + 1` once the component has
ticked `N` times past `t₀`.

Two components with one seed publish one stream, so independent sources take
distinct seeds.

`μ` and the scale are broadcast to one type, the parameter `V` and the
output's, `Float64` or an `SArray` of `Float64`, so a scalar pairs with an
array. Over an `SArray` the components are independent.

Exactly one of `σ` and `psd` is given. Neither or both is refused as an
`ArgumentError`. Halve a one-sided density before passing it as `psd`.

# Keywords

- `seed`: the non-negative integer the stream is drawn from.
- `μ`: the mean, zero in the scale's shape when left at `nothing`.
- `σ`: the standard deviation per sample, at any period.
- `psd`: the two-sided intensity `Q` of the white noise the samples stand for,
  with `σ² = Q/Δt` at the [component](@ref g-component)'s own period `Δt`.

types.name: Redstone.Library.Integrator
types.docstring:
Integrator(; x0 = 0.0, reset::Bool = false) -> Integrator

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes the time integral of
its input.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) holds one continuous state
`x`, starting at `x0`, with `ẋ = u` and `y = x`, published from
[stage 1](@ref g-stage-function). The component therefore has no
[feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough). A `Float64` state follows the scalar of a
`Dual` [activation](@ref g-activation), so the component linearizes as it
integrates.

A wire names its input `u` and its output `y` by [face](@ref g-face), as in
`"integrator/u"`.

With `reset`, the component gains a second input, the `Bool` `reset`, and its
data input keeps the face `u`, as in `"integrator/u"` and `"integrator/reset"`.
A rising edge of `reset` writes `x0` into `x`, through one
[state event](@ref g-state-event), `reset`. The event is
[non-localized](@ref g-non-localized), so the reset lands on the
[boundary](@ref g-boundary) where `reset` rises. Under
[edge semantics](@ref g-edge-semantics), holding `reset` resets once, and a
second rising edge resets again.

A `reset` published from a mode rises only on a boundary, so no reset is late. A
reset driven by a continuous quantity takes it through a [`Comparator`](@ref),
which localizes the crossing. A `reset` already holding at `t₀` fires at
[boundary zero](@ref g-boundary-zero).

The state, the input `u` and the output `y` share one type, the parameter `V`,
`Float64` or an `SArray` of `Float64`, taken from `Float64.(x0)`, an array
converted to an `SArray`, so an integer, a `Float32` or a plain array `x0`
qualifies.

# Keywords

- `x0`: the initial value of `x`, and the value a reset writes.
- `reset`: `true` for the form with the `reset` input.

See also [`LimitedIntegrator`](@ref), [`DiscreteIntegrator`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.LimitedIntegrator
types.docstring:
LimitedIntegrator(; lower, upper, x0 = zero(lower), localized::Bool = true, reset::Bool = false) -> LimitedIntegrator

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes the time integral of
its input, held between two limits.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) integrates its input `u` into
one continuous state `x`, with `ẋ = u` while free and `ẋ = 0` while saturated.
It stops integrating at a limit rather than clamping its output. The output
`out` publishes `x` from [stage 1](@ref g-stage-function).

Four [state events](@ref g-state-event) move the mode, the field `m`, a signed
`Int8` code with the sign of the limit in force. The code is `-1` at `lower`,
`0` free and `+1` at `upper`.

- `hit_upper` and `hit_lower` fire when `x` reaches a limit. They are
  [localized](@ref g-localized). They write `x` to the limit exactly and
  saturate.
- `leave_upper` and `leave_lower` fire when `u` turns strictly back into the
  range, and they free the component. An input of exactly zero at a limit keeps
  it saturated.

An input that turns outward again after a leave, even within the same step,
stops the component on the limit.

The output `saturation` publishes the code from stage 1, so it has no
[feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough). It serves an anti-windup consumer, such as a
controller that gates its integrator on the code. The code changes only when an
event fires, and so only on a declared [boundary](@ref g-boundary).

`localized` picks how the leave events fire. With `true`, a departure ends the
step at the input's zero crossing, at the cost of root-finding and a split step.
With `false`, the leave events are
[non-localized](@ref g-non-localized), and a departure costs neither. It fires
at the first boundary after `u` points back into the range, at the latest the
end of that step. `x` stays on the limit until then. It then carries an
offset of about `a h² / 2` at most, to leading order in `h`, with `a` the
input's slope at its zero crossing and `h` the step.

Over an `SArray`, the limits and the codes are componentwise, and `saturation`
publishes an `SArray` of `Int8` of the same shape. The integrator declares one
copy of each event per component, named `hit_upper_1` to `hit_upper_N`, then
`hit_lower_i`, `leave_upper_i` and `leave_lower_i`. Each copy acts on its own
component.

An `x0` outside the limits is clamped at [boundary zero](@ref g-boundary-zero),
and the initial mode agrees with the initial input.

`reset = true` adds the `Bool` input `reset`, so the inputs `u` and `reset` are
named. It also adds one `reset` event, however wide the component is. As on the
[`Integrator`](@ref), the event is non-localized on the flag, so it fires
once per rising edge. Its handler writes `x0`, clamped to the limits, and the
code that value earns. A reset onto a limit therefore lands saturated, and frees
at that boundary if `u` points back into the range. A reset inside lands free,
whatever the mode was.

`x0`, `lower` and `upper` broadcast to one shape and type, the parameter `V`,
`Float64` or an `SArray` of `Float64`, so a scalar limit pairs with a vector and
integer values qualify. A `lower` not below `upper`, componentwise over an
`SArray`, is refused as an `ArgumentError`.

# Keywords

- `lower`: the lower limit, below `upper`.
- `upper`: the upper limit.
- `x0`: the initial value of `x`, and the value a reset writes.
- `localized`: `true` for localized leave events, `false` for non-localized
  ones.
- `reset`: `true` to add the input `reset` and its event.

See also [`LimitedDoubleIntegrator`](@ref), [`DiscreteLimitedIntegrator`](@ref),
[`Integrator`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.FirstOrderLag
types.docstring:
FirstOrderLag(; τ, x0 = 0.0) -> FirstOrderLag

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes its input through a
first-order lag of time constant `τ`.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) holds one continuous state `x`
from `x0`. Its input is `u` and its output `y`, with `ẋ = (u - x) / τ` and
`y = x`, published from [stage 1](@ref g-stage-function). The state follows the
scalar of a `Dual` [activation](@ref g-activation), so the lag linearizes to
`A = -1/τ` and `B = 1/τ`.

For a scalar signal the component is
[`TransferFunction`](@ref)`(num = (1,), den = (τ, 1), u0 = x0)`. The component
stays for `SArray` signals, for `x0` in the signal's own coordinates and for
the spelling.

The state, the input `u`, the output `y` and `τ` share one type, the parameter
`V`, `Float64` or an `SArray` of `Float64`, the broadcast of `τ` and `x0` to one
shape, so a scalar `τ` pairs with a vector `x0` and integer values qualify. Over
an `SArray` the lag is componentwise, each component at its own `τ`. A `τ` that
is not positive in every component is refused as an `ArgumentError`. `τ` stays
at `Float64` whatever scalar the model runs at.

# Keywords

- `τ`: the time constant, positive.
- `x0`: the initial value of `x`.

types.name: Redstone.Library.StateSpace
types.docstring:
StateSpace(; A::AbstractMatrix, B::AbstractMatrix, C::AbstractMatrix,
               D::AbstractMatrix = zeros(size(C, 1), size(B, 2)),
               x0 = zeros(size(A, 1))) -> StateSpace

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that runs a linear system given in
state-space form.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) holds one continuous state `x`
from `x0`, and its input is `u` and its output `y`:

    ẋ = A x + B u
    y = C x + D u

The state is an `SVector` at every size. `u` is a `Float64` when `n_u` is one
and an `SVector{n_u, Float64}` otherwise, and `y` likewise by `n_y`.

`D` picks the component's [feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough) class, which
[`AbstractLinearSystem`](@ref) explains. A zero `D` publishes `y` from
[stage 1](@ref g-stage-function). The component then breaks an
[algebraic loop](@ref g-algebraic-loop) as [`FirstOrderLag`](@ref) does. A
nonzero `D` publishes it from stage 2, so a loop closed on the component through
a memoryless path is refused as `AlgebraicCycle`.

The matrices are kept at `Float64`. The state and the [ports](@ref g-port)
follow the scalar of a `Dual` [activation](@ref g-activation), so the component
linearizes to its own matrices.

Each matrix is any `AbstractMatrix` of reals, stored at full shape as an
`SMatrix` of `Float64`, so integer entries qualify. A matrix that does not fit
the others is refused as an `ArgumentError`, and so is an `x0` of the wrong
length. An `A` of size zero is refused likewise, since a component with no state
is a gain.

# Keywords

- `A`: the `n_x × n_x` state matrix.
- `B`: the `n_x × n_u` input matrix.
- `C`: the `n_y × n_x` output matrix.
- `D`: the `n_y × n_u` direct matrix, zero by default.
- `x0`: the initial state, in the coordinates of `A`, a vector of length `n_x`,
  or a real when `n_x` is one.

See also [`TransferFunction`](@ref), [`DiscretizedStateSpace`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.TransferFunction
types.docstring:
TransferFunction(; num, den, u0 = 0.0) -> TransferFunction
    TransferFunction(; zeros = (), poles, gain = 1.0, u0 = 0.0) -> TransferFunction

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that runs a single-input,
single-output linear system given by its transfer function in `s`.

The transfer function is

    G(s) = (num[1] sᵐ + … + num[end]) / (den[1] sⁿ + … + den[end])

from the input `u` to the output `y`, both `Float64`. The
[library component](@ref g-library-component) keeps the coefficients and holds
their realization in controllable canonical form, a [`StateSpace`](@ref).

The second spelling gives the roots in place of the coefficients,

    G(s) = gain (s - zeros[1]) … (s - zeros[end]) / ((s - poles[1]) … (s - poles[end]))

with `zeros` empty by default. A root is real or complex, and the complex ones
come in conjugate pairs, so that the coefficients are real. The component keeps
the coefficients the roots expand to. Mixing the two spellings is refused as an
`ArgumentError`, as is a set of roots that is not closed under conjugation, and
more zeros than poles.

There is no `x0`. The component starts at rest, or, with `u0` given, at the
steady state for the constant input `u0`, where `y` is `G(0) u0`.

The degrees pick the component's [feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough) class, which
[`AbstractLinearSystem`](@ref) explains. A numerator of lower degree than
the denominator publishes `y` from [stage 1](@ref g-stage-function). The
component then breaks an [algebraic loop](@ref g-algebraic-loop). One of equal
degree publishes it from stage 2.

Four spellings are refused as an `ArgumentError`. A denominator of fewer than
two coefficients has order zero, which makes a gain. A numerator longer than the
denominator is improper. The third is a leading denominator coefficient of zero.
The fourth is a nonzero `u0` over a denominator whose constant coefficient is
zero, a pole at the origin, which has no steady state.

# Keywords

- `num`: the numerator's coefficients, highest power first, as a tuple or a
  vector of reals.
- `den`: the denominator's coefficients, highest power first, likewise.
- `zeros`: the zeros, real or complex, as a tuple or a vector; none by default.
- `poles`: the poles, likewise.
- `gain`: the factor on the numerator, `1.0` by default.
- `u0`: the constant input whose steady state the component starts at, `0.0` for
  rest.

See also [`DiscreteTransferFunction`](@ref),
[`DiscretizedTransferFunction`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.Relay
types.docstring:
Relay(; lower, upper, off = zero(lower), on = one.(lower)) -> Relay

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes one of two values,
switched by its input with hysteresis.

Its input is `u` and its output `y`. The output publishes `off` or `on` by the
mode, the field `m`, from [stage 1](@ref g-stage-function). The mode is an
`Int8` code, `0` off and `1` on.

Two [state events](@ref g-state-event) move the mode. `switch_on` fires when `u`
rises to `upper` while off, and `switch_off` when `u` falls strictly below
`lower` while on. At `lower == upper` an input exactly on the threshold therefore
reads on. Both are [localized](@ref g-localized).

`y` reads no input, so the [library component](@ref g-library-component) has no
[feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough). A relay closing a feedback loop therefore
makes no [algebraic loop](@ref g-algebraic-loop).

The four values and both [ports](@ref g-port) share one type, the parameter `V`,
`Float64` or an `SArray` of `Float64`, the four keywords' broadcast to one
shape, so a scalar pairs with a vector and integer values qualify. `y` is
[pinned](@ref g-walked) at `V`. It carries zero partials under every
[activation](@ref g-activation).

Over an `SArray`, the thresholds, the values and the codes are componentwise.
The relay declares `N` copies of the two events, one per component, named
`switch_on_1` to `switch_on_N`, then `switch_off_i`. Each copy acts on its own
component.

The relay starts off. An input already at or above `upper` at `t₀` turns the
relay on at [boundary zero](@ref g-boundary-zero), and an input between the
thresholds leaves it off, which is the hysteresis itself.

A `lower` above `upper` is refused as an `ArgumentError`.

# Keywords

- `lower`: the threshold `u` falls below for the relay to switch off, at most
  `upper`.
- `upper`: the threshold `u` rises to for the relay to switch on.
- `off`: the value `y` publishes while off.
- `on`: the value `y` publishes while on.

types.name: Redstone.Library.UnitDelay
types.docstring:
UnitDelay(s0) -> UnitDelay

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes its input from the
previous [tick](@ref g-tick).

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) is the native `z⁻¹` of the
discrete [tier](@ref g-tier). A wire names its input `u` and its output `y` by
[face](@ref g-face), `"delay/u"` and `"delay/y"`.

The output publishes the stored value `s` from [stage 1](@ref g-stage-function),
`y = s`, and `s0` at the first publication. Each tick stores the input for the
next one, `s⁺ = u`. The [store](@ref g-store) and both [ports](@ref g-port)
share one type, the parameter `V`, the type of `s0`, an isbits type or a
`Symbol`, as the store requires.

It breaks an [algebraic loop](@ref g-algebraic-loop), and that is a modelling
decision. Placed in a continuous loop, it moves the signal onto the discrete
tier and inserts a zero-order hold over the [component](@ref g-component)'s own
period, a multiple of [`Δt_base`](@ref g-dt_base).

See also [`Delay`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.DiscreteIntegrator
types.docstring:
DiscreteIntegrator(; s0 = 0.0, reset::Bool = false) -> DiscreteIntegrator

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes the forward-Euler
integral of its input.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) holds one
[store](@ref g-store) value from `s0`, the field `s`. Its input is `u` and its
output `y`.

Each [tick](@ref g-tick) advances the store by forward Euler,
`s⁺ = s + Δt u`, and the output publishes `y = s` from
[stage 1](@ref g-stage-function). The component therefore breaks an
[algebraic loop](@ref g-algebraic-loop) as [`UnitDelay`](@ref) does. `Δt` is the
[component](@ref g-component)'s own period, so the integral is per second at any
rate.

`reset = true` adds the `Bool` input `reset`, so the inputs `u` and `reset` are
named. The reset is a level. At every tick where `reset` reads true, the update
writes `s0` in place of the sum. The output at the reset tick still publishes
the integral before it, and the next tick's output publishes `s0`. The
continuous [`Integrator`](@ref) resets on the flag's rising edge instead, as an
[event](@ref g-state-event).

The discrete [tier](@ref g-tier) never follows the scalar of an
[activation](@ref g-activation), so under a `Dual` activation the component
holds its last value.

The state, the input `u` and the output `y` share one type, the parameter `V`,
`Float64` or an `SArray` of `Float64`, taken from `Float64.(s0)`, an array
converted to an `SArray`, so an integer, a `Float32` or a plain array `s0`
qualifies.

# Keywords

- `s0`: the initial value of `s`, and the value a reset writes.
- `reset`: `true` to add the input `reset`.

See also [`DiscreteLimitedIntegrator`](@ref), [`Integrator`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.RateLimiter
types.docstring:
RateLimiter(; rising, falling = rising, s0 = 0.0) -> RateLimiter

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes its input with its rate
of change bounded per [tick](@ref g-tick).

The output `y` follows the input `u`, moving at most `rising Δt` up and
`falling Δt` down per tick. `Δt` is the [component](@ref g-component)'s own
period. One [store](@ref g-store) value, the field `s`, holds the previous
output, and each tick stores `y`:

    y = s + clamp(u - s, -falling Δt, rising Δt)

Over an `SArray` the slew is componentwise.

`y` reads `u`, so the [library component](@ref g-library-component) has
[feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough). A loop closed on it through a memoryless path
is refused as `AlgebraicCycle`. A [`UnitDelay`](@ref) after the component breaks
that loop, and lags the input by one tick at every rate.

The rates, the state and both [ports](@ref g-port) share one type, the parameter
`V`, `Float64` or an `SArray` of `Float64`, the broadcast of `rising`, `falling`
and `s0` to one shape, so a scalar rate pairs with a vector `s0` and integer
values qualify. Over an `SArray` each component slews at its own rates. A
`rising` or a `falling` that is not positive in every component is refused as an
`ArgumentError`. The rates stay at `Float64` whatever scalar the model runs at.

# Keywords

- `rising`: the largest rise per second, positive.
- `falling`: the largest fall per second, positive.
- `s0`: the previous output at the first tick, so the output at `t₀` is already
  one slew step from it.

types.name: Redstone.Library.DiscreteStateSpace
types.docstring:
DiscreteStateSpace(; A::AbstractMatrix, B::AbstractMatrix, C::AbstractMatrix,
                       D::AbstractMatrix = zeros(size(C, 1), size(B, 2)),
                       s0 = zeros(size(A, 1))) -> DiscreteStateSpace

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that runs a linear system given in
discrete state-space form.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) holds one
[store](@ref g-store) value from `s0`, the field `s`, advanced once per
[tick](@ref g-tick), and its input is `u` and its output `y`:

    s⁺ = A s + B u
    y  = C s + D u

The keywords, the shapes, the storage, the [ports](@ref g-port) and the refusals
are those of [`StateSpace`](@ref), with `s0` in place of its `x0`.

The [feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough) class of
[`AbstractDiscreteLinearSystem`](@ref) is also that of `StateSpace`. A zero `D`
publishes `y` from [stage 1](@ref g-stage-function). The component then breaks
an [algebraic loop](@ref g-algebraic-loop). A nonzero `D` publishes it from
stage 2.

The discrete [tier](@ref g-tier) never follows the scalar of an
[activation](@ref g-activation), so under a `Dual` activation the component
holds its last value.

The matrices presuppose the period they were designed at. That period is the
one the component's [rate scope](@ref g-rate-scope) gives it, bound at
deployment after the component is built, so the component cannot check it. A
system that should follow its period is a [`DiscretizedStateSpace`](@ref).

# Keywords

- `A`: the `n_x × n_x` state matrix.
- `B`: the `n_x × n_u` input matrix.
- `C`: the `n_y × n_x` output matrix.
- `D`: the `n_y × n_u` direct matrix, zero by default.
- `s0`: the initial state, in the coordinates of `A`, a vector of length `n_x`,
  or a real when `n_x` is one.

types.name: Redstone.Library.DiscreteTransferFunction
types.docstring:
DiscreteTransferFunction(; num, den, u0 = 0.0) -> DiscreteTransferFunction
    DiscreteTransferFunction(; zeros = (), poles, gain = 1.0, u0 = 0.0) -> DiscreteTransferFunction

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that runs a single-input, single-output
linear system given by its transfer function in `z`.

The transfer function is

    G(z) = (num[1] zᵐ + … + num[end]) / (den[1] zⁿ + … + den[end])

with the coefficients highest power of `z` first, as [`TransferFunction`](@ref)
takes them in `s`. This is not the `z⁻¹` convention of `filter(b, a)`, which
agrees with it only when the degrees are equal.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) keeps the coefficients and
holds their realization in controllable canonical form, a
[`DiscreteStateSpace`](@ref). The degrees pick the
[feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough) class of
[`AbstractDiscreteLinearSystem`](@ref) as for `TransferFunction`.

The component starts at rest, or, with `u0` given, at the steady state for the
constant input `u0`, where `y` is `G(1) u0`.

The keywords, the two spellings and the refusals are those of
`TransferFunction`, the roots in `z`, save that the pole with no steady state is
at `z = 1`. A nonzero `u0` is refused as an
`ArgumentError` over a denominator whose coefficients sum to zero within `1e-12`
of the sum of their magnitudes. A designed denominator such as `(1, -0.7, -0.3)`
misses an exact zero by rounding.

The coefficients presuppose the period they were designed at, which the
component cannot check, as for `DiscreteStateSpace`.

# Keywords

- `num`: the numerator's coefficients, highest power of `z` first, as a tuple or
  a vector of reals.
- `den`: the denominator's coefficients, highest power of `z` first, likewise.
- `zeros`: the zeros in `z`, real or complex, as a tuple or a vector; none by
  default.
- `poles`: the poles in `z`, likewise.
- `gain`: the factor on the numerator, `1.0` by default.
- `u0`: the constant input whose steady state the component starts at, `0.0` for
  rest.

See also [`DiscretizedTransferFunction`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.DiscretizedStateSpace
types.docstring:
DiscretizedStateSpace(continuous::StateSpace) -> DiscretizedStateSpace
    DiscretizedStateSpace(; A::AbstractMatrix, B::AbstractMatrix, C::AbstractMatrix,
                          D::AbstractMatrix = zeros(size(C, 1), size(B, 2)),
                          x0 = zeros(size(A, 1))) -> DiscretizedStateSpace

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that runs a continuous state-space
system through a zero-order hold at each [tick](@ref g-tick).

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) runs the [`StateSpace`](@ref)
`continuous`, or the one its keywords build, on the discrete
[tier](@ref g-tier). At each tick it takes the zero-order hold

    A_d = e^{A Δt}        B_d = (∫₀^Δt e^{Aτ} dτ) B

with `C` and `D` unchanged. The hold is exact for an input held constant over
each period, so the samples are the continuous system's own.

`Δt` is the [component](@ref g-component)'s own period, so the component follows
the rate its [rate scope](@ref g-rate-scope) gives it. It carries no period of
its own, where a [`DiscreteStateSpace`](@ref) presupposes one.

The keywords and their refusals are those of `StateSpace`. The
[feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough) class, the [ports](@ref g-port) and `x0` are
the continuous component's, `x0` in its coordinates.

The discrete tier never follows the scalar of an
[activation](@ref g-activation), so under a `Dual` activation the component
holds its last value.

# Keywords

- `A`: the `n_x × n_x` state matrix.
- `B`: the `n_x × n_u` input matrix.
- `C`: the `n_y × n_x` output matrix.
- `D`: the `n_y × n_u` direct matrix, zero by default.
- `x0`: the initial state, in the coordinates of `A`, a vector of length `n_x`,
  or a real when `n_x` is one.

See also [`DiscretizedTransferFunction`](@ref),
[`AbstractDiscreteLinearSystem`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.DiscretizedTransferFunction
types.docstring:
DiscretizedTransferFunction(; num, den, u0 = 0.0) -> DiscretizedTransferFunction
    DiscretizedTransferFunction(; zeros = (), poles, gain = 1.0, u0 = 0.0) -> DiscretizedTransferFunction

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that runs a continuous transfer
function through a zero-order hold at each [tick](@ref g-tick).

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) takes the transfer function in
`s` of [`TransferFunction`](@ref), with its keywords in either spelling, its
refusals and its start at rest or at `G(0) u0`. It runs it on the discrete
[tier](@ref g-tier) through the zero-order hold of
[`DiscretizedStateSpace`](@ref). The hold is taken at each
tick. It spans `Δt`, the [component](@ref g-component)'s own period. The degrees
pick the [feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough) class of
[`AbstractDiscreteLinearSystem`](@ref) as for `TransferFunction`.

The hold keeps the feedthrough class and matches the step response at the
samples. A design that wants Tustin's frequency response discretizes externally
and uses [`DiscreteTransferFunction`](@ref).

# Keywords

- `num`: the numerator's coefficients, highest power of `s` first, as a tuple or
  a vector of reals.
- `den`: the denominator's coefficients, highest power of `s` first, likewise.
- `zeros`: the zeros in `s`, real or complex, as a tuple or a vector; none by
  default.
- `poles`: the poles in `s`, likewise.
- `gain`: the factor on the numerator, `1.0` by default.
- `u0`: the constant input whose steady state the component starts at, `0.0` for
  rest.

types.name: Redstone.Library.DiscreteLimitedIntegrator
types.docstring:
DiscreteLimitedIntegrator(; lower, upper, s0 = zero(lower), reset::Bool = false) -> DiscreteLimitedIntegrator

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes the forward-Euler
integral of its input, held between two limits.

Its input is `u`. Each [tick](@ref g-tick) advances the one
[store](@ref g-store) value, the field `s`, from `s0` as
`s⁺ = clamp(s + Δt u, lower, upper)`. The output `out` publishes `s` from
[stage 1](@ref g-stage-function).

A second output, `saturation`, publishes the `Int8` code of
`LimitedIntegrator`, read off the state, also from stage 1. The code is `1` at
`upper`, `-1` at `lower` and `0` between. At a limit with the input already
pointing inward, the code reads saturated until the next tick moves the state
off.

Over an `SArray`, the limits and the codes are componentwise, and `saturation`
publishes an `SArray` of `Int8` of the same shape.

`reset = true` adds the `Bool` input `reset`, so the inputs
`u` and `reset` are named. It is the level reset of
[`DiscreteIntegrator`](@ref). The update writes `s0`, clamped, at every tick
where the flag reads true.

`s0`, `lower` and `upper` broadcast to one shape and type, the parameter `V`,
`Float64` or an `SArray` of `Float64`, so a scalar limit pairs with a vector and
integer values qualify. A `lower` not below `upper`, componentwise over an
`SArray`, is refused as an `ArgumentError`.

# Keywords

- `lower`: the lower limit, below `upper`.
- `upper`: the upper limit.
- `s0`: the initial value of `s`, and the value a reset writes, clamped.
- `reset`: `true` to add the input `reset`.

See also [`DiscreteIntegrator`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.Delay
types.docstring:
Delay(; K::Int, v0 = 0.0, taps::Bool = false) -> Delay

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes its input from `K`
[ticks](@ref g-tick) before.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) is the delay line, the `z⁻ᴷ`
of the discrete [tier](@ref g-tier). The output `y` publishes the input `u` from
`K` ticks ago, and `v0` at the first `K` publications.
It publishes from [stage 1](@ref g-stage-function). The [store](@ref g-store) is
a ring of `K` values and a cursor.

It breaks an [algebraic loop](@ref g-algebraic-loop) as [`UnitDelay`](@ref)
does in either form, and that is a modelling decision. Placed in a continuous
loop, it moves the signal onto the discrete tier and inserts a zero-order hold
over the [component](@ref g-component)'s own period, a multiple of
[`Δt_base`](@ref g-dt_base).

`K` counts ticks of the component's own period, so the user picks it from the
rate the component declares. `K = 1` is `UnitDelay` in keyword spelling. A
smaller `K` is refused as an `ArgumentError`.

`v0` is a value of the signal, copied into every slot of the ring. It is not the
initial store, so it is not `UnitDelay`'s `s0`. The ring's values, the input
`u` and the output `y` share one type, the parameter `V`, `Float64` or an
`SArray` of `Float64`, taken from `Float64.(v0)`, an array converted to an
`SArray`, so an integer, a `Float32` or a plain array `v0` qualifies.

`taps = true` adds a second output, `taps`, so the outputs `y` and `taps` are
named. It publishes the last `K` inputs as an `SVector{K, V}`, newest first,
with `v0` in the slots no tick has filled yet. `taps[1]` is the input from one
tick ago and `taps[K]` the one from `K` ticks ago, which is `y`. It serves a
law over the window written in a stage body, a moving median or a minimum over
the last `K` samples. A FIR filter is a [`DiscreteTransferFunction`](@ref)
instead. The taps publish from stage 1 as `y` does.

# Keywords

- `K`: the delay in ticks, at least 1.
- `v0`: the value published before `K` ticks have passed.
- `taps`: `true` to add the output `taps`.

types.name: Redstone.Library.Freeze
types.docstring:
Freeze{V}() -> Freeze{V}

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes its input with its
partials dropped, so no derivative passes through it.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) is the declared stop-gradient.
Its output `y` is its input `u` with its partials dropped,
[pinned](@ref g-walked) at the parameter `V`, a `Float64` or an `SArray` of
`Float64`. A producer that walks may therefore feed a [`Pinned`](@ref) input
[entry](@ref g-entry) through it. At [nominal](@ref g-nominal) it is the
identity. Every Jacobian along the path then reads a zero coupling, which is the
modelling decision the component states.

Any other `V` is refused as a `TypeError` where `Freeze{V}` is written. The
component drops one `Dual` layer, so at a nested `Dual` an input that carries
partials is refused at build as `ConformanceFailure`.

types.name: Redstone.Library.PID
types.docstring:
PID(; Kp, Ki = 0.0, Kd = 0.0, τd = 0.1, Tt = Inf, u_min = -Inf, u_max = Inf,
          b = 1.0, c = 0.0, hold::Bool = false, tracking::Bool = false) -> PID

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that runs a PID controller with
anti-windup.

The inputs are `r` and `y`, with the error `e = r - y`. Two outputs come from
[stage 2](@ref g-stage-function), `u_raw` and `u`, its clamp to
`[u_min, u_max]`:

    u_raw = Kp (b r - y) + q - Kd (w - yf) / τd

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) holds two continuous states.
`q` is the integral term. `yf` is the weighted measurement `w = y - c r` through
a lag, `ẏf = (w - yf) / τd`. One law moves the integral term:

    q̇ = Ki ε + (ref - u_raw) / Tt

Two independent keywords, `hold` and `tracking`, each adding inputs, fill the
slots `ε` and `ref` over the error `e` by the table of
[`AbstractAntiWindupController`](@ref).

`hold = true` adds two inputs. `saturation` is an `Int8` code such as a
[`LimitedIntegrator`](@ref) publishes for the path downstream. It gates the
error by sign. `engaged` is a `Bool` that reads true while the component is in
command. Not engaged, the error is gated to zero whatever the code. Without
tracking, a component not engaged freezes. `q` then holds while the own clamp is
free and back-calculates against it otherwise.

`tracking = true` adds the input `v`, a value the path delivered or the selected
command. It takes the place of the own `u` as the correction's reference. With
the hold, `v` is the reference only while the component is limited or not
engaged, and `u` while it is free. A component not in command therefore follows
the selected command at rate `1/Tt` and engages without a bump. It chases a
moving `v` with lag `Tt`, so a component out of command wants a short `Tt`.

The default `Tt = Inf` follows nothing. `tracking = true` with a `Tt` given as a
value and infinite in any channel is therefore refused as an `ArgumentError`.
Tracking needs `Tt` spelled, or given as `AsPort()`, which leaves it to the
component tree to keep finite.

A `u_min` above `u_max`, both given as values, is refused as an `ArgumentError`.
So is a `τd` or a `Tt` given as a value and not positive in every channel. The
default `Tt = Inf` passes.

`q` holds the integral term in output units, with `Ki` inside the integral, so
a change in `Ki` alters only future accumulation.

The setpoint weights `b` and `c` multiply `r` alone, and the integral's error
stays `e`. `b` acts in the proportional term and `c` in the derivative's
weighted measurement. Their defaults, `b = 1` and `c = 0`, put the derivative on
the measurement, so a step in `r` makes no kick. `c = 1` puts it on the error.

The defaults make the plain spelling a P controller, with `Ki = Kd = 0` and
infinite limits. They also set `Tt = Inf`, which switches the correction off.

The parameters, the inputs `r`, `y` and `v`, the outputs `u` and `u_raw` and
the states share one type, the parameter `V`, `Float64` or an `SArray` of
`Float64`, the broadcast of the nine keywords given as values. Over an `SArray`
the law is componentwise, and `saturation` is an `SArray` of `Int8` of `V`'s
shape and `engaged` one of `Bool`.

The nine keywords given as values broadcast to one `V`, so a scalar pairs with a
vector and integer values qualify. A vector PID with uniform gains spells at
least one keyword as a vector, `Kp = @SVector fill(2.0, 3)`.

Any of the nine parameters may be an input [port](@ref g-port) in place of a
field, spelled `Kp = AsPort()` with [`AsPort`](@ref). The port is named for the
parameter and typed `V`. It takes no part in the shape, so when every
value-carrying keyword is a port, `V` is `Float64`. Under a `Dual`
[activation](@ref g-activation), a parameter given as a port carries partials,
so a linearization sees the coupling through the port. A component tree that
wants it frozen at its plain `Float64` value routes the port through
[`Freeze`](@ref).

`u` is a stage-2 output, so every input makes a
[feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough) edge, whether `y_direct` reads it or not. A
tracking input wired from a memoryless clamp of the component's own `u` is
refused as an `AlgebraicCycle` classified [artificial](@ref g-algebraic-loop).
`v` serves a value published from state, such as a stateful actuator's position.
A parameter port computed memorylessly from `u` closes a cycle too, artificial
for `Ki` and `Tt`, which only the derivative reads, and real for the others. One
read from a state is fine.

# Keywords

- `Kp`: the proportional gain.
- `Ki`: the integral gain, inside the integral.
- `Kd`: the derivative gain.
- `τd`: the time constant of the derivative's lag, positive.
- `Tt`: the time constant of the correction, `Inf` to switch it off.
- `u_min`: the lower limit of `u`.
- `u_max`: the upper limit of `u`.
- `b`: the setpoint weight in the proportional term.
- `c`: the setpoint weight in the derivative's weighted measurement.
- `hold`: `true` to add the inputs `saturation` and `engaged`.
- `tracking`: `true` to add the input `v`.

See also [`DiscretePID`](@ref), [`AbstractPID`](@ref), [`LQRTracker`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.DiscretePID
types.docstring:
DiscretePID(; Kp, Ki = 0.0, Kd = 0.0, τd = 0.1, Tt = Inf, u_min = -Inf, u_max = Inf,
                  b = 1.0, c = 0.0, hold::Bool = false, tracking::Bool = false) -> DiscretePID

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that runs a PID controller with
anti-windup.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) takes the parameters,
defaults, [ports](@ref g-port) and law of [`PID`](@ref) to the discrete
[tier](@ref g-tier). Two [store](@ref g-store) fields stand in for its
continuous states. `q` is the integral term, and `yf` is the weighted
measurement `w = y - c r` through a lag. A third, `saturated`, holds its code.
`Δt` is the [component](@ref g-component)'s own period.

The inputs are `r` and `y`, with the error `e = r - y`. Two outputs come from
[stage 2](@ref g-stage-function), `u_raw` and `u`, its clamp to
`[u_min, u_max]`:

    u_raw = Kp (b r - y) + q - Kd (w - yf) / (τd + Δt)

Each [tick](@ref g-tick) moves the lag by backward Euler,
`yf⁺ = yf + Δt (w - yf) / (τd + Δt)`. It moves the integral term by forward
Euler and the correction's exact step:

    q⁺ = q + Δt Ki ε + β (ref - u_raw),    β = 1 - exp(-Δt / Tt)

The two anti-windup axes fill the slots `ε` and `ref` by the table of
[`AbstractAntiWindupController`](@ref).

`hold` adds the inputs `saturation` and `engaged`. A component not engaged
without tracking freezes. `tracking` adds the input `v`. With the hold, the
reference falls back to `u` while the component is free. All of this is as in
`PID`. The setpoint weights `b` and `c` multiply `r` alone, as in `PID`, and the
integral's error stays `e`.

`tracking = true` with a `Tt` given infinite in any channel is refused as an
`ArgumentError`, as in `PID`. So is a `u_min` above `u_max`, both given as
values, and so is a `τd` or a `Tt` given as a value and negative in any channel.
Either may be zero.

The parameters, the inputs `r`, `y` and `v`, the outputs `u` and `u_raw` and the
store fields `q` and `yf` share one type, the parameter `V`, `Float64` or an
`SArray` of `Float64`. Over an `SArray` the law is componentwise, as in `PID`.
The nine keywords given as values broadcast to one `V` by the rule of `PID`. A
scalar therefore pairs with a vector, and a uniform vector gain spells one
keyword as a vector, `Kp = @SVector fill(2.0, 3)`.

Any parameter may be an input port, spelled `Kp = AsPort()` with
[`AsPort`](@ref), typed `V` and outside the shape. Under a `Dual`
[activation](@ref g-activation) the discrete tier does not run and holds its
`Float64` values, so a linearization sees no coupling through the port and a
[`Freeze`](@ref) on it changes nothing.

The backward Euler lag is stable at every period, and `τd = 0` is legal. `yf` is
then the previous weighted measurement, and the D term the backward difference
`(w - yf) / Δt`.

`β` is the exact step of the correction's relaxation over one period, so every
`Tt` is stable. `Tt = Inf` switches the correction off. `Tt = 0` is legal and
brings `u_raw` to the reference plus the tick's integral step `Δt Ki ε` by the
next tick, the clamping scheme as the limit of tracking. Not engaged with
tracking, `Tt = 0` lands `u_raw` on the tick's `v` one tick later, exact for a
constant `v` while `r` and `y` hold.

A third output, `saturated`, publishes the `Int8` code of the component's own
clamp, an `SArray` of `Int8` of `V`'s shape over an array. The code is `1` with
`u_raw` at or above `u_max`, `-1` at or below `u_min` and `0` between. The
component stores the code from `u_raw` at the tick and publishes it from stage 1
at the next. It is therefore one tick stale, and flips only on a tick
[boundary](@ref g-boundary).

The code serves the hold of an outer controller in a cascade, wired to its input
`saturation`. The outer controller's integrator takes one extra step before the
hold engages. As a stage-1 port the code closes no cycle through the outer
controller's `u`.

A tracking input wired from a memoryless clamp of the component's own `u` is
refused as an `AlgebraicCycle`, as for `PID`, but classified real. A parameter
port computed memorylessly from `u` closes a cycle likewise.

# Keywords

- `Kp`: the proportional gain.
- `Ki`: the integral gain, inside the integral.
- `Kd`: the derivative gain.
- `τd`: the time constant of the derivative's lag, `0` for the backward
  difference.
- `Tt`: the time constant of the correction, `Inf` to switch it off and `0` to
  correct within one tick.
- `u_min`: the lower limit of `u`.
- `u_max`: the upper limit of `u`.
- `b`: the setpoint weight in the proportional term.
- `c`: the setpoint weight in the derivative's weighted measurement.
- `hold`: `true` to add the inputs `saturation` and `engaged`.
- `tracking`: `true` to add the input `v`.

See also [`AbstractPID`](@ref), [`DiscreteLQRTracker`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.LQRTracker
types.docstring:
LQRTracker(; K_fbk, K_fwd, K_int = zero(SMatrix{NU, NZ, Float64}),
               x_trim = zero(SVector{NX, Float64}), u_trim = zero(SVector{NU, Float64}),
               z_trim = zero(SVector{NZ, Float64}), Tt = Inf, u_min = -Inf, u_max = Inf,
               hold::Bool = false, tracking::Bool = false) -> LQRTracker
    LQRTracker{NX, NU, NZ}(; K_fbk, K_fwd, K_int = zero(SMatrix{NU, NZ, Float64}),
                           x_trim = zero(SVector{NX, Float64}), u_trim = zero(SVector{NU, Float64}),
                           z_trim = zero(SVector{NZ, Float64}), Tt = Inf, u_min = -Inf, u_max = Inf,
                           hold::Bool = false, tracking::Bool = false) -> LQRTracker{NX, NU, NZ}

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that runs an LQR tracker about a trim
point, with anti-windup.

The inputs are `x`, the plant state, `z`, the command variables, and `z_ref`,
their reference. Two outputs come from [stage 2](@ref g-stage-function), `u_raw`
and `u`, its clamp to `[u_min, u_max]` per channel:

    u_raw = u_trim + K_fwd (z_ref - z_trim) - K_fbk (x - x_trim) + q

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) holds one continuous state,
the field `x`, written `q` below. It is the integral term in output units, one
channel per control input. One law moves it:

    q̇ = ε + (ref - u_raw) / Tt

The two anti-windup axes of [`PID`](@ref), each adding inputs, fill the slots
`ε` and `ref` over the integrator input `e = K_int (z_ref - z)`. They fill them
channel by channel, by the table of [`AbstractAntiWindupController`](@ref).

`hold = true` adds two inputs. `saturation`, a code per channel from the path
downstream, gates each channel whose code agrees with the sign of its integrator
input. `engaged`, a flag per channel that reads true in command, zeroes the
integrator input of a channel not engaged whatever its code. Without tracking, a
channel not engaged freezes, its own clamp's correction alone moving it.

`tracking = true` adds the input `v` as the correction's reference in place of
the own `u`. With the hold, `v` is the reference in a channel only while it is
limited or not engaged. A channel not engaged therefore converges to `v` at rate
`1/Tt` and engagement is bumpless. The own clamp is the correction's, and
`Tt = Inf` switches it off.

Tracking with a `Tt` given as a value and infinite in any channel is refused as
an `ArgumentError`, as for `PID`. A `u_min` above `u_max`, both given as values,
is refused as an `ArgumentError`, and so is a `Tt` given as a value and not
positive in every channel. The default `Tt = Inf` passes.

The [ports](@ref g-port) are each an `SVector` at every size. `x` is an
`SVector{NX, Float64}`, `z` and `z_ref` are `SVector{NZ, Float64}`, and `u`,
`u_raw` and `v` are `SVector{NU, Float64}`. `saturation` is an
`SVector{NU, Int8}` and `engaged` an `SVector{NU, Bool}`.

Any of the nine parameters may be an input port in place of a field, spelled
`K_fbk = AsPort()` with [`AsPort`](@ref) and typed as the field would be, an
`SMatrix{NU, NX, Float64, NU * NX}` for `K_fbk`. That is how a gain schedule
reaches the component. Under a `Dual` [activation](@ref g-activation), the port
carries partials. A component tree that wants it frozen at its plain `Float64`
value routes it through [`Freeze`](@ref).

The first form reads `NX`, `NU` and `NZ` off the values given, `K_fbk` first,
then `K_fwd`, `K_int` and the trims. The second, the explicit spelling, takes
the sizes and the same keywords. A matrix or a vector that does not fit the
sizes read is refused as an `ArgumentError`. A size no value carries, every
carrier a port or left at its default, is refused likewise, naming the explicit
spelling.

`u` is a stage-2 output, so every input makes a
[feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough) edge, whether `y_direct` reads it or not. An
`x` assembled from what the plant publishes from state, and a `z` selected from
the same, close no loop. A `z_ref` computed memorylessly from the component's
own `u` closes an `AlgebraicCycle` classified real, since the direct law reads
it. A tracking input wired from a memoryless clamp of `u` closes one classified
[artificial](@ref g-algebraic-loop), since only the derivative reads it. A
parameter port computed memorylessly from `u` closes a cycle too, artificial for
`K_int` and `Tt` and real for the others.

The component publishes no saturation code. The gains are designed outside, from
[`trim!`](@ref Redstone.trim!) and [`linearize`](@ref Redstone.linearize).

`K_int` and the trims default to zero. `Tt`, `u_min` and `u_max` are each a real
broadcast to an `SVector{NU, Float64}`, or a vector of length `NU`. Integer
entries qualify.

# Keywords

- `K_fbk`: the `NU × NX` feedback gain, any `AbstractMatrix` of reals stored as
  an `SMatrix{NU, NX, Float64}`.
- `K_fwd`: the `NU × NZ` feedforward gain, stored likewise.
- `K_int`: the `NU × NZ` integral gain, stored likewise, zero for the tracker
  without integral action.
- `x_trim`: the plant state at trim, a vector of length `NX`.
- `u_trim`: the control input at trim, a vector of length `NU`.
- `z_trim`: the command variables at trim, a vector of length `NZ`.
- `Tt`: the time constant of the correction per channel, `Inf` to switch it off.
- `u_min`: the lower limit of `u` per channel.
- `u_max`: the upper limit of `u` per channel.
- `hold`: `true` to add the inputs `saturation` and `engaged`.
- `tracking`: `true` to add the input `v`.

See also [`DiscreteLQRTracker`](@ref), [`AbstractLQRTracker`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.DiscreteLQRTracker
types.docstring:
DiscreteLQRTracker(; K_fbk, K_fwd, K_int = zero(SMatrix{NU, NZ, Float64}),
                       x_trim = zero(SVector{NX, Float64}), u_trim = zero(SVector{NU, Float64}),
                       z_trim = zero(SVector{NZ, Float64}), Tt = Inf, u_min = -Inf, u_max = Inf,
                       hold::Bool = false, tracking::Bool = false) -> DiscreteLQRTracker
    DiscreteLQRTracker{NX, NU, NZ}(; K_fbk, K_fwd, K_int = zero(SMatrix{NU, NZ, Float64}),
                                   x_trim = zero(SVector{NX, Float64}), u_trim = zero(SVector{NU, Float64}),
                                   z_trim = zero(SVector{NZ, Float64}), Tt = Inf, u_min = -Inf, u_max = Inf,
                                   hold::Bool = false, tracking::Bool = false) -> DiscreteLQRTracker{NX, NU, NZ}

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that runs an LQR tracker about a trim
point, with anti-windup.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) takes the parameters,
defaults, [ports](@ref g-port), outputs and law of [`LQRTracker`](@ref) to the
discrete [tier](@ref g-tier). A [store](@ref g-store) field `q` stands in for
its continuous state, and a second, `saturated`, holds its code. `Δt` is the
[component](@ref g-component)'s own period.

The inputs are `x`, `z` and `z_ref`. Two outputs come from
[stage 2](@ref g-stage-function), `u_raw` and `u`, its clamp to
`[u_min, u_max]` per channel:

    u_raw = u_trim + K_fwd (z_ref - z_trim) - K_fbk (x - x_trim) + q

Each [tick](@ref g-tick) moves the integral term by forward Euler and the
correction's exact step:

    q⁺ = q + Δt ε + β (ref - u_raw),    β = 1 - exp(-Δt / Tt)

The two anti-windup axes fill the slots `ε` and `ref` over the integrator input
`e = K_int (z_ref - z)`. They fill them channel by channel, by the table of
[`AbstractAntiWindupController`](@ref).

`hold` adds the inputs `saturation` and `engaged`. A channel not engaged without
tracking freezes. `tracking` adds the input `v`. With the hold, the reference
falls back to `u` in each channel that is free. All of this is as in
`LQRTracker`.

`tracking = true` with a `Tt` given infinite in any channel is refused as an
`ArgumentError`, as in `LQRTracker`. So is a `u_min` above `u_max`, both given
as values, and so is a `Tt` given as a value and negative in any channel.

Every `Tt` is stable. `Tt = Inf` switches the correction off. `Tt = 0` is legal
and brings `u_raw` to the reference plus the tick's integral step `Δt ε` by the
next tick. A channel not engaged with tracking lands `u_raw` on the tick's `v`
one tick later, exact for a constant `v` while the direct terms hold.

The ports, the nine parameters and their types, the [`AsPort`](@ref) spelling,
the size inference and the explicit spelling, the second form, are those of
`LQRTracker`, and so are the refusals.

A third output, `saturated`, publishes the `Int8` code of the component's own
clamp per channel at `SVector{NU, Int8}`. The code is `1` with `u_raw` at or
above `u_max`, `-1` at or below `u_min` and `0` between. The component stores
the code from `u_raw` at the tick and publishes it from stage 1 at the next. It
is therefore one tick stale, and flips only on a tick
[boundary](@ref g-boundary).

The code serves the hold of an outer controller in a cascade, wired to its input
`saturation`, each channel reaching a scalar consumer through
[`Unpack`](@ref)`{Int8, NU}`. The outer integrator takes one extra step before
the hold engages. As a stage-1 port the code closes no cycle through the outer
component's `u`.

`u` is a stage-2 output, so every input makes a
[feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough) edge, as for `LQRTracker`. A `z_ref` or a
tracking input computed memorylessly from the component's own `u` is refused as
an `AlgebraicCycle` classified real. A parameter port computed memorylessly from
`u` closes a cycle likewise.

# Keywords

- `K_fbk`: the `NU × NX` feedback gain.
- `K_fwd`: the `NU × NZ` feedforward gain.
- `K_int`: the `NU × NZ` integral gain.
- `x_trim`: the plant state at trim.
- `u_trim`: the control input at trim.
- `z_trim`: the command variables at trim.
- `Tt`: the time constant of the correction per channel, `Inf` to switch it off
  and `0` to correct within one tick.
- `u_min`: the lower limit of `u` per channel.
- `u_max`: the upper limit of `u` per channel.
- `hold`: `true` to add the inputs `saturation` and `engaged`.
- `tracking`: `true` to add the input `v`.

See also [`AbstractLQRTracker`](@ref), [`DiscretePID`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.Fn
types.docstring:
Fn{U, Y}(f) -> Fn{U, Y}
    Fn{U}(f) -> Fn{U, U}

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes a function of its one
input as its one output.

The one input, `u`, is typed `U`, and the one output, `y`, is typed `Y`, the
two parameters as written. It publishes `y = f(u)`, and a wire names its
[ports](@ref g-port) as in `"fn/u"` and `"fn/y"`. `Fn{U}(f)` is `Fn{U, U}(f)`.
The port types are never read off `f`, so `f` returns a `Y`. Nothing converts
at nominal, so a value of another type is refused as `ConformanceFailure`, at
build for the value the build reads and as a `StepError` carrying it on a later
[frame](@ref g-frame).

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) is the one-input
[`Junction`](@ref) with its input bare. It spells a step between two children
that wires cannot, such as a unit conversion or a sign flip. It is not a gain.
Each instance is a separate [component](@ref g-component) and costs a build
entry, a cell, a gather and a scatter, so a one-line expression is cheaper
inside the consumer's own stage.

`f` runs under every [activation](@ref g-activation) of the build, a `Dual` one
included. A `Y` wrapped in [`Pinned`](@ref) declares an output that carries no
partials. `f` must then drop them itself, as [`Freeze`](@ref) does for a
`Float64` or an `SArray`. An `f` that passes them on is refused as
`ConformanceFailure` by the first build, linearization or trim that runs it
under a `Dual` activation.

The function holds no state and declares no [events](@ref g-state-event), so a
discontinuity written into it lands wherever it falls inside a step, as in a
`Junction`.

types.name: Redstone.Library.Fields
types.docstring:
Fields{V}() -> Fields{V}

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes each field of its
struct input as an output of its own.

The one input, `u`, is typed `V`, a struct or `NamedTuple` type with at least
one field. The outputs take the field names of `V`, each typed as its field
and publishing that field of `u`. A wire names the input as in `"fields/u"` and
an output as in `"fields/pose"`. The
[library component](@ref g-library-component) is stateless and unbundles one
level only, so a field that is itself a struct is one output.

A wire takes a [port](@ref g-port) whole, so the component is how a wired
consumer takes less than a struct-valued port. A read takes a field directly
through the [leaf address](@ref g-leaf-address) and needs no component.

Any other `V` is refused as an `ArgumentError`. A `Float64` and an `SArray` are
among them, and [`Unpack`](@ref) splits an `SVector`.

types.name: Redstone.Library.Select
types.docstring:
Select{V, K}() -> Select{V, K}

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes one of its inputs,
picked by an enum input.

`K` is an enum type. The component has one input per instance of `K`, named
after the instance and typed `V`, and the input `select`, a `K`. The one output,
`y`, is typed `V`. It is the input that `select` names, so over
`@enum Leg CLIMB CRUISE` a wire reads `"sel/CRUISE"`. The
[library component](@ref g-library-component) is stateless.

The output reads every input. A `select` wired from a memoryless function of the
output therefore closes an [algebraic loop](@ref g-algebraic-loop), which the
build refuses as `AlgebraicCycle`. A linearization takes no partials through
`select`, and the picked input's partials pass through.

The component declares no [event](@ref g-state-event), so the jump in the output
lands where `select` changes. A `select` published from a mode, or held between
[ticks](@ref g-tick), changes on a [boundary](@ref g-boundary) and the jump is
clean. One computed from a continuous quantity inside a
[stage body](@ref g-stage-function) changes inside a step and smears that step.

An abstract `K`, or an enum with an instance named `select`, is refused as an
`ArgumentError`.

See also [`Switch`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.Sequence
types.docstring:
Sequence(; times, values, localized::Bool = true) -> Sequence

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes a schedule of values,
switching at each of its breakpoints.

Its one output, `y`, publishes `values[1]` before `times[1]`, `values[k + 1]`
from `times[k]` until `times[k + 1]`, and the last value from the last
breakpoint on. The [library component](@ref g-library-component) has no inputs
and no continuous state, and is a [`Step`](@ref) at one breakpoint.

Its one mode, the field `m`, counts the breakpoints passed. One
[state event](@ref g-state-event), `advance`, fires when `t` reaches the next
breakpoint and sets the count to every breakpoint at or before `t`.

`values` broadcast to one shape and type, the parameter `V`, `Float64` or an
`SArray` of `Float64`, so a scalar pairs with a vector and integer values
qualify. The output is [pinned](@ref g-walked) at `V`, so it carries zero
partials under every [activation](@ref g-activation).

`localized` picks the detection policy.
[Localized](@ref g-localized), each breakpoint ends the step at its crossing, so
two breakpoints inside one step each land at their own time.
[Non-localized](@ref g-non-localized), each jump lands on the first
[boundary](@ref g-boundary) at or after its breakpoint, and breakpoints passed
inside one step advance together there.

The breakpoints at or before `t₀` are passed at
[boundary zero](@ref g-boundary-zero), and the output starts at the value that
follows them.

`times` that do not ascend strictly, or a count of `values` other than `N + 1`,
are refused as an `ArgumentError`.

# Keywords

- `times`: the `N` breakpoints, strictly ascending, any times.
- `values`: the `N + 1` values.
- `localized`: `true` for localized breakpoints, `false` for non-localized
  ones.

types.name: Redstone.Library.Backlash
types.docstring:
Backlash(; width, s0 = 0.0) -> Backlash

A discrete [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that holds its output inside a deadband
about it and moves it with the input outside.

The output `y` holds while the input `u` stays within half of `width` of it,
and follows `u` at that offset once `u` moves further. One [store](@ref g-store)
value, the field `s`, holds the previous output, and each [tick](@ref g-tick)
stores `y`:

    y = clamp(s, u - width / 2, u + width / 2)

Over an `SArray` the deadband is componentwise.

`y` reads `u`, so the [library component](@ref g-library-component) has
[feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough). A loop closed on it through a memoryless path
is refused as `AlgebraicCycle`. A [`UnitDelay`](@ref) after the component breaks
that loop, and lags the output by one tick at every rate.

The width, the state and both [ports](@ref g-port) share one type, the parameter
`V`, `Float64` or an `SArray` of `Float64`, the broadcast of `width` and `s0` to
one shape, so a scalar width pairs with a vector `s0` and integer values
qualify. A `width` that is not positive in every component is refused as an
`ArgumentError`. The width stays at `Float64` whatever scalar the model runs at.

# Keywords

- `width`: the full width of the deadband, positive.
- `s0`: the previous output at the first tick, so the output at `t₀` already
  sits within half a width of the input.

See also [`RateLimiter`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.LimitedDoubleIntegrator
types.docstring:
LimitedDoubleIntegrator(; lower, upper, q0 = zero(lower), v0 = zero(lower), localized::Bool = true) -> LimitedDoubleIntegrator

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes the double time
integral of its input, its position held between two limits.

The [library component](@ref g-library-component) is a mechanical stop. It holds
a named continuous state of two leaves, the position `q` and the velocity `v`.
Its one input `u` is the acceleration, with `q̇ = v` and `v̇ = u` while free and
both zero while saturated. The outputs `out` and `velocity` publish `q` and `v`
from [stage 1](@ref g-stage-function).

Four [state events](@ref g-state-event) move the mode, the field `m`, a signed
`Int8` code with the sign of the limit in force. The code is `-1` at `lower`,
`0` free and `+1` at `upper`.

- `hit_upper` and `hit_lower` fire when `q` reaches a limit. They are
  [localized](@ref g-localized). They write `q` to the limit exactly, zero `v`
  and saturate, so the stop absorbs the impact.
- `leave_upper` and `leave_lower` fire when `u` turns strictly back into the
  range, and they free the component from rest. An input of exactly zero at a
  limit keeps it saturated.

A component that reaches a limit while `u` already points back into the range
saturates and frees at the same [boundary](@ref g-boundary), so it leaves the
limit from rest. An input that turns outward again after a leave, even within
the same step, stops the component on the limit.

The output `saturation` publishes the code from stage 1, so it has no
[feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough). It serves an anti-windup consumer. The code
changes only when an event fires, and so only on a declared boundary.

`localized` picks how the leave events fire. With `true`, a departure ends the
step at the input's zero crossing, at the cost of root-finding and a split step.
With `false`, the leave events are
[non-localized](@ref g-non-localized), and a departure costs neither. It fires
at the first boundary after `u` points back into the range, at the latest the
end of that step. `q` and `v` stay on the limit until then. From then on `v`
carries an offset of about `a h² / 2` at most, to leading order in `h`, with `a`
the input's slope at its zero crossing and `h` the step. `q` carries an offset
that grows by as much per unit time. The next limit removes both.

Over an `SArray`, the limits, the leaves and the codes are componentwise,
`velocity` publishes an `SArray` of the same shape and `saturation` one of
`Int8`. The integrator declares one copy of each event per component, named
`hit_upper_1` to `hit_upper_N`, then `hit_lower_i`, `leave_upper_i` and
`leave_lower_i`. Each copy acts on its own component.

A `q0` outside the limits is clamped at [boundary zero](@ref g-boundary-zero)
with `v` zeroed. A `q0` on a limit with `v0` pointing back into the range starts
free and keeps `v0`. At rest there, the initial mode agrees with the initial
input.

`q0`, `v0`, `lower` and `upper` broadcast to one shape and type, the parameter
`V`, `Float64` or an `SArray` of `Float64`, so a scalar limit pairs with a
vector and integer values qualify. A `lower` not below `upper`, componentwise
over an `SArray`, is refused as an `ArgumentError`.

# Keywords

- `lower`: the lower limit on `q`, below `upper`.
- `upper`: the upper limit on `q`.
- `q0`: the initial value of `q`.
- `v0`: the initial value of `v`.
- `localized`: `true` for localized leave events, `false` for non-localized
  ones.

See also [`LimitedIntegrator`](@ref), [`Integrator`](@ref).

types.name: Redstone.Library.Comparator
types.docstring:
Comparator(; threshold = nothing, lower = nothing, upper = nothing,
               localized::Bool = true) -> Comparator

A continuous [primitive](@ref g-primitive) that publishes whether its input has
risen past a threshold, with optional hysteresis.

Its input is `u`, and its one output, `y`, is a `Bool` published from
[stage 1](@ref g-stage-function) by the mode, the field `m`. The mode is an
`Int8` code, `0` below and `1` above. Two [state events](@ref g-state-event)
move it. `switch_on` fires when `u` rises to `upper` while below, and
`switch_off` when `u` falls strictly below `lower` while above. At
`lower == upper` the [library component](@ref g-library-component) is a plain
threshold and publishes `u ≥ threshold`. Between them it holds its last value,
which is the hysteresis.

The output is [pinned](@ref g-walked) at `Bool`, and it changes only when an
event fires, so only on a [boundary](@ref g-boundary). It is the declared way to
feed a [`Switch`](@ref)'s `select` from a continuous quantity, and the switch's
jump then lands where the comparator's event lands. `y` reads no input, so the
component has no [feedthrough](@ref g-feedthrough).

`localized` picks the detection policy.
[Localized](@ref g-localized), each switch ends the step at the crossing.
[Non-localized](@ref g-non-localized), each switch lands on the first
boundary that observes it.

Over an `SArray`, the thresholds and the codes are componentwise, and `y` is an
`SArray` of `Bool` of the same shape. The comparator declares `N` copies of the
two events, one per component, named `switch_on_1` to `switch_on_N`, then
`switch_off_i`. Each copy acts on its own component.

The component starts below. An input already at or above `upper` at `t₀`
switches the component on at [boundary zero](@ref g-boundary-zero).

A plain comparator takes `threshold` alone. Hysteresis takes `lower` and `upper`
together and without `threshold`. Any other combination of the three keywords,
or a `lower` above `upper`, is refused as an `ArgumentError`.

`lower` and `upper` broadcast to one shape and type, the parameter `V`, which
the input `u` shares, `Float64` or an `SArray` of `Float64`, so a scalar pairs
with a vector and integer values qualify.

# Keywords

- `threshold`: the threshold of a plain comparator, which sets both `lower` and
  `upper`.
- `lower`: the threshold `u` falls below for the output to turn `false`, at most
  `upper`, componentwise over an `SArray`.
- `upper`: the threshold `u` rises to for the output to turn `true`.
- `localized`: `true` for localized switches, `false` for non-localized
  ones.

See also [`Relay`](@ref), [`Switch`](@ref).
